title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. Γ̂^+_{0,3} is the profinite completion of PSL(2,Z) ≅ Z/3 * Z/2 = ⟨ρ,σ | ρ^3 = σ^2 = 1⟩. It sits in an exact sequence 1 → Π_{0,3} → Γ̂^+_{0,3} → Γ̂_3 = S_3 → 1. Here Π_{0,3} is the profinite free group F̂_2, i.e. π_1 of P^1 − {0,1,∞}; Γ(2)/±1 inside PSL(2,Z) is the discrete model. Geometrically, Γ̂^+_{0,3} is the orbifold π_1 of the j-line, seen as [(P^1−{0,1,∞})/S_3].

The lemma being proved. The previous page states: any surjection p: Γ̂^+_{0,3} → S_3 is conjugate to the canonical one, so its kernel is Π_{0,3}. Hence every group automorphism of Γ̂^+_{0,3} preserves Π_{0,3}. Grothendieck calls this the key step towards proving that every L-automorphism of Γ̂^+_{0,3} is inner.

Proof completed on this page.
- Take a (continuous) homomorphism p out of Z/3 * Z/2 whose image has order ≥ 4. Then p(ρ) has order exactly 3 and p(σ) order exactly 2: if p(ρ) = 1 the image has order ≤ 2, and if p(σ) = 1 it has order ≤ 3.
- Suppose the image is S_3. Then p(ρ) is a 3-cycle ρ̇^{±1}. Conjugating by the transposition σ̇_∞, which inverts ρ̇, we may assume p(ρ) = ρ̇.
- p(σ) is one of the three transpositions σ̇_0, σ̇_1, σ̇_∞. Conjugating by ρ̇^{±1}, which fixes ρ̇ and permutes the transpositions cyclically, we may assume p(σ) = σ̇_∞.
- So p equals the canonical map up to an inner automorphism of S_3. The argument is correct and elementary; profinitely it uses only that continuous maps to finite groups are fixed by the images of the topological generators.

Definition introduced. For an 'L-group' Π (a discrete or profinite group with orientation module and peripheral/inertia data, as made precise on the next page), Grothendieck defines its 'Teichmüller group':
- either Out_L(Π), the group of L-outer automorphisms;
- or, preferably, Out_L(Π^+), where Π^+ (index 1 or 2) consists of the g whose inner automorphism int(g) is orientation-preserving ('direct').

The 'envisaged property' of Γ̂^+_{0,3} is that its direct Teichmüller group is trivial, i.e. every L-automorphism is inner. Combined with the previous page, this would characterize Γ̂^+_{0,3} up to non-unique isomorphism. The next page gives the companion property for the discrete L-group Γ_{0,3} ≅ GL(2,Z)/±1: every L-automorphism of Γ^+_{0,3} is induced by a unique element of Γ_{0,3}. He suggests this may characterize the discrete case. This is an abstract analogue of Dehn–Nielsen–Baer: the mapping class group as Out of π_1 preserving peripheral structure and orientation.
errors: The finite-group lemma is correct. The two '[?]' verbs are probably 'inverse ρ̇' (conjugation by σ̇_∞) and 'fixe ρ̇' / 'amène sur σ̇_∞' (conjugation by ρ̇^{±1}); the logic holds either way.

The 'envisaged property' (direct Teichmüller group of the PROFINITE Γ̂^+_{0,3} trivial, i.e. every direct L-automorphism inner) appears false if L-automorphisms are only required to preserve inertia/orientation data. The argument runs as follows.
- Γ̂^+_{0,3} is the geometric orbifold π_1 of the j-line over Q̄.
- Elements of Gal(Q̄/Q^ab) have trivial cyclotomic character. They preserve all inertia classes with exponent 1, so they act by direct L-automorphisms.
- Suppose such automorphisms were inner. Restricted to the characteristic subgroup Π_{0,3} = F̂_2, their image in Out(F̂_2) would then lie in the image of S_3, a group of order ≤ 6.
- But Gal(Q̄/Q) → Out(F̂_2) is injective (Belyi), so Gal(Q̄/Q^ab) has infinite image there.
- Equivalently, elements of GT_1 act on B̂_3/Z ≅ Γ̂^+_{0,3} by σ1 ↦ σ1, σ2 ↦ f^{-1}σ2 f, which preserves the cusp class. This step was not checked.
The property is true for discrete PSL(2,Z): Out(PSL(2,Z)) = Z/2, the non-trivial class reversing orientation. That fits his hedge on the next page that it is 'peut-être caractéristique des L-groupes discrets'. Unless his notion of profinite L-automorphism carries extra structure not visible here, the profinite claim as stated conflicts with Belyi's theorem.

ideas.what: Any surjection Z/3*Z/2 (or its profinite completion) onto S_3 is conjugate to the canonical one, so the kernel F̂_2 = Π_{0,3} is characteristic in PSL(2,Ẑ)^
ideas.modern_name: characteristic nature of the congruence subgroup Γ(2)/±1 (resp. its profinite closure) in PSL(2,Z)^

ideas.what: Teichmüller group of an 'L-group' := group of (orientation-preserving) outer automorphisms preserving peripheral/inertia structure, defined abstractly for discrete or profinite groups
ideas.modern_name: abstract mapping class group via Dehn–Nielsen–Baer; profinite outer automorphism groups preserving inertia (Out^*, GT-type groups, profinite Teichmüller groups)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dehn–Nielsen–Baer (discrete); Ihara, Drinfeld, Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Boggi, Hoshi–Mochizuki (profinite variants)
ideas.where_published: Teichmüller tower ideas in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche; the precise 'L-groupe' formalism is not known to me in published form

ideas.what: Proposed rigidity: trivial direct Teichmüller group as characterizing Γ̂^+_{0,3} (profinite) and Γ_{0,3} ≅ GL(2,Z)/±1 (discrete)
ideas.modern_name: outer-automorphism rigidity / group-theoretic characterization of orbifold fundamental groups (anabelian-type)
ideas.usually_credited_to: related work: Nakamura, Hoshi–Mochizuki (outer automorphisms of profinite orbicurve groups)

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates (as a goal) that every direct L-automorphism of profinite PSL(2,Z) is inner, i.e. a trivial profinite Teichmüller group for the j-line orbifold. This seems to contradict the faithful outer Galois action (Belyi) restricted to Gal(Q̄/Q^ab), or equivalently GT_1. The page documents an evolving stance: on the next page he retreats to the discrete case.
missed.quote: La propriété envisagée de 𝔖_{0,3}^+ est que son groupe de Teichmüller "direct" est réduit à 1.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest for how Grothendieck separated discrete rigidity from profinite (Galois/GT) non-rigidity in the Longue Marche notes. It is not a new mathematical result.

deep.surprise_reason: The lemma is elementary. The abstract 'Teichmüller group of an L-group' as Out preserving peripheral and orientation data is a natural Dehn–Nielsen–Baer-style notion that later literature developed (GT, profinite Out groups). The interesting point is the apparent tension between the stated profinite rigidity and Belyi's theorem, which reads as an exploratory slip rather than a missed result.
transcription_corrections: The group symbol transcribed as 𝔖_{0,3}^+ is almost certainly the same Γ̂^+_{0,3} (hatted G/Γ) as on the previous page, not a symmetric-group fraktur S.
'[?]' after 'conjuguer par σ̇_∞, qui' is probably 'inverse ρ̇'; the later 'qui [?] σ̇_∞' likely means conjugation by ρ̇^{±1} brings σ̇_0/σ̇_1 to σ̇_∞ (or 'fixent ρ̇').
'homom. p [?] de' — the [?] is likely just 'p' or 'p :'.
'L-automorphismes extérieurs' is written 'L-automor-phismes' across a line break; content is correct.
